alexander: Hey folks — need quick help. I just registered a domestic partnership and want to add my partner to medical + dental. What docs do I need to upload, what’s the deadline, and when will coverage be effective? Any payroll/tax gotchas I should know about?
Benefits Bot: Congrats on your life event! Please submit a qualifying life event in the Benefits Portal within 30 days of the event date. Link: https://benefits.redwoodinc/example-enroll. See "Required Documents" section for partner proof.
Maya (People Ops): Congrats, @alexander 🎉. Short answers: submit within 30 days to avoid gaps; required docs vary by insurer but we typically accept: marriage certificate OR domestic partnership affidavit, plus one supporting document (joint lease, joint bank stmt, proof of shared address). If you don’t have a marriage cert, upload the completed Domestic Partnership Affidavit (PDF) + a photo ID for the partner.
Maya (People Ops): Effective date: if you enroll within 30 days, coverage is usually effective retroactive to the event date OR the 1st of the month following the event depending on your plan carrier. We’ll confirm with the carrier after you submit. Payroll deductions change at the next payroll cycle after the carrier processes the enrollment (often 1–2 pay cycles).
alexander: Appreciate it. Any chance you can paste the exact list of acceptable docs? Want to avoid back-and-forth. Also, how long until they mail an ID card?
Maya (People Ops): Sure — acceptable docs (pick one from A and one from B if DP):
A: legal marriage certificate OR completed Domestic Partnership Affidavit (signed)
B (one of): joint lease or mortgage, joint bank statement (last 3 months), joint utility bill, shared health insurance or tax return, or a government document showing shared address.
Maya (People Ops): ID cards: electronic ID is usually available within 48–72 hrs after carrier confirms enrollment; physical cards 7–14 business days. If you need proof sooner for an appointment, request an electronic ID via the portal and we can also request expedited verification.
Priya: I added my partner last month — timeline was: submitted docs online on Wed, carrier confirmed in 3 business days, electronic ID same day, physical in 10 days, payroll change showed up after 2 pay cycles. Also FYI: if you're adding a domestic partner (not legally married) the employer-paid portion is often considered imputed income — my paycheck showed a small tax adjustment. Payroll@redwood explained it pretty fast.
Maya (People Ops): Good note, @Priya. For taxability specifics we always advise checking with payroll or your tax advisor. If you want, we can estimate the imputed income amount for you; email benefits@redwood.com with your plan choice and we’ll run numbers.
alexander: Perfect. I’ll gather docs today. One more: if I already had an appointment last week and the charge hit before I enrolled, can we get that covered retroactively?
Maya (People Ops): Possibly. If you enroll within 30 days of the event, many carriers will apply retroactive coverage to the event date and consider claims incurred during that period. For an existing claim, keep the itemized bill + proof of event date and submit a retroactive enrollment request to benefits@redwood.com — we’ll coordinate with the carrier. No guarantees (depends on carrier rules) but we’ll escalate.
alexander: Thank you! Sending docs now.
Maya (People Ops): Received — I’ll ack once I submit to the carrier. If anything else needed I’ll ping you here. :thumbsup:
Benefits Bot: Enrollment submission received by People Ops. Reference #BP-2026-8421. You will get a carrier confirmation email once processed.
